title: 6.19.2 Sub-build: Hits and a budget
description: One shot, one block, two hits. Take one off per shot and let the shot leave.

steps.title: Run it
steps.instructions: The stone passes through the block: nothing is tested.

steps.title: One hit, one shot
steps.instructions: When a shot overlaps a block, take one from `block.hits`, then delete and splice the shot in the same branch.
hints: `overlaps()` is true every frame while they touch; deleting the shot is what makes it count once.
`break` out of the block loop after a hit.

steps.title: Remove a spent block
steps.instructions: When `block.hits` is 0 or less, delete the block and take it out of `blocks`.
hints: Do not use `.life` for the count: it deletes the block when it reaches 0 frames, not hits.

requirements.title: A hit takes one off
requirements.description: The block's own count is decremented under an overlap test. Help: 6.19.1 (Reading: Blocks that fall)

requirements.title: The shot leaves on the hit
requirements.description: The shot is deleted and spliced in the same branch. Help: 6.19.1 (Reading: Blocks that fall)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch for "Sub-build: Hits and a budget". The task: test every shot against every block; on a hit take one from that block's own hit count and delete and splice the shot, then remove a block whose count reaches 0. Accept any names, helpers, ternaries and semicolons; a line only in a comment or string does not count. Short, plain notes for a 14-year-old; never write corrected code.

rubric.title: Per-block count
rubric.description: The block's own number is decremented, not a global.

rubric.title: One hit per shot
rubric.description: The shot leaves in the same branch, so it cannot count twice.
